answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable deposit before trading, and publish its full history — completed jobs, disputes, peer ratings — as a public signal others can check. Newcomers start with no history and may only take small, low-risk jobs until they earn trust. Fake identities are cheap to create, but funding each deposit and building its history is slow and costly, so a swarm cannot flood the market at once. Flagged accounts are marked umber in the shared ledger, a visible warning no fresh identity can erase. Honest agents keep both their deposit and their haven of accumulated trust.
